RFC4301-4.1-1.note: IKE Child SA install asserts Mode==tunnel on both SAs and the OSPFv3 installer asserts Mode==transport on every SA, so both modes are proven; single-polarity annotated

RFC4301-4.1-12.note: Re-judged pass 6. The unit now asserts what Linux actually reads for inbound source matching on a transport-mode SA: the state selector x->sel (xfrm_selector_match in __xfrm_policy_check), read back from the kernel for the ff02::5 and ff02::6 states found by (group, SPI), with source ::/0; a control AH state installed with selector source fe80::2/128 is read back first as a /128, so the read-back discriminates a pinned source from the wildcard. The props-source :: assertion is kept and correctly described as the outbound address check, not claimed. Doc comment, PREVENTS line and failure text now name the right mechanism. Producer read: buildIPsecSA sets Sel.Src to ospfWildcardNet(). Each probe runs in its own user+net namespace (no cross-test state). Revert record of buildIPsecSA observed red; author's overlay pinning Sel.Src also went red. single-polarity holds: multicast SAs exist only as RFC 4552 manual config, which always sets the indication, so no refusal path exists. Full ospf package -race green.

RFC4301-4.1-2.note: TestChildSAInstallsInDataplane asserts every installed policy is tunnel mode; single-polarity annotated

RFC4301-4.1-3.note: every IKE peer SA is asserted modeTunnel; OSPFv3 transport SAs fall under the security-gateway-acting-as-host exception; single-polarity annotated

RFC4301-4.1-4.note: inbound and outbound SA of one IKE pair both asserted modeTunnel, so the pair is same-mode; single-polarity annotated

RFC4301-4.1-6.note: Judged on the path where Ze has multicast SAs (R24): the RFC 4552 manual OSPFv3 installer (buildIPsecInterfaceSAs/buildIPsecSA) run through onInterfaceUp over the real XFRM backend in a rootless user+net namespace; the lookup is netlink XFRM_MSG_GETSA against the kernel SAD (xfrm_state_lookup, the function XFRM input uses), not a mock (run by the judge 2026-09-30: child ran, not skipped). Positive: ff02::5 and ff02::6 share one SPI and each (group, SPI) lookup returns that group's own SA, i.e. step 2 (SPI + destination) of the section 4.1 search resolves an Any-Source Multicast group SA. Negative: after a control lookup, ff02::5 under an unconfigured SPI and the configured SPI to ff02::1 map to no SA (step 3 fails, packet has no SA). Step 1 (SPI+dst+src) is vacuous: Ze builds no source-specific multicast SA. Caveat recorded, not a finding against the tests: the ff02::1 case rests on Linux identifying the fe80:: unicast SA by (dst, SPI, proto) rather than the section 4.1 SPI(+protocol) identifier, so a literal step 3 would match that unicast SA; the stray-SPI case alone carries the negative without that reading. Records: revert buildIPsecSA, both polarities observed red.

RFC4301-4.1-9.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after c85342c940). Section 4.1: "The receiver MUST process the packets from the different SAs without prejudice." The two dataplane SAD boundary units changed only by the deleted RFC4301-4.4.2.1-3 tag lines; their bodies are identical, and the engine units are byte-identical. Judged on the positive under owner ruling 5: TestRFC4301ParallelSAsWithOneSelectorAreEachReceived installs two Child SAs on one selector pair through createFirstChildSA over real XFRM in a rootless netns and delivers an in-selector packet on SA1, SA2, then SA1 again; a per-SA template or reqid mismatch, or shared replay state that dropped the sibling's packets, goes red. The builder positive asserts two SAD entries with distinct SPIs 0x1000 and 0x2000 from xfrmStateFromParams. The negatives (TestRFC4301ParallelSAsAreHeldToTheOneSharedPolicy, which proves the 4.4.1-10 post-decryption SPD check, and the SAD refusal unit, which proves an unbuildable SA installs nothing) stay supplementary: no receive-side input can inject prejudiced processing.

RFC4301-4.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent auditor, after d64411a639 and 08bfef9ee7). Section 4.2: "Note: A compliant implementation MUST NOT allow instantiation of an ESP SA that employs both NULL encryption and no integrity algorithm." d64411a639 makes NULL encryption reachable for IKE Child SAs, so every instantiation path was re-read for NULL + no integrity. Config: parseESPProposal requires a hash for every non-AEAD cipher and null is non-AEAD (TestIntegrityOnlyESPConfig, 'hash is required'). Negotiation: initiator NegotiateESP runs espProposalComplete, which now refuses ENCR_NULL beside AUTH_NONE (RFC 4303 Section 3.2 quoted above it; TestIntegrityOnlyESPRefusals asserts ErrProposalIncomplete); responder matchOfferedESP passes a non-zero integID for a non-AEAD local proposal and espProposalMatches requires the offer to contain it. XFRM: planStateAlgos gives non-AEAD ESP Crypt+Auth and xfrmAuthNames holds no '' or 'none', so TestRFC4301ESPNullEncryptionWithoutIntegrityIsRefused (refused, no state) and the NULL+sha256 positive stand. VPP: vppCryptoAlg now names null as CRYPTO_ALG_NONE, so the refusal moved to vppIntegAlg, whose default arm refuses '' and 'none' beside a non-AEAD cipher; the changed TestRFC4301VPPESPNullEncryptionWithoutIntegrityIsRefused keeps the control install (1 message) and asserts ErrNotSupported with zero VPP messages for '' and 'none'. Dropped from it: the null+sha256 refusal case and the vppCryptoAlg('null') error assertion, both of which asserted behaviour RFC 4303 Section 1 now requires to be absent; that is a correction, not a weakening (owner-approval debt row for 08bfef9ee7 is open). OSPF manual SAs unchanged (validateIPsecInterface both polarities). All units pass at HEAD with and without -tags ze_vpp. Finding, no verdict change: the new VPP negative record breaks vppIntegAlg with a panic, which would also redden the control install, so it shows the unit reaches vppIntegAlg rather than that the default arm is the refusal; a record making vppIntegAlg return INTEG_ALG_NONE for '' would discriminate the refusal itself.

RFC4301-4.4.1-1.note: Child SA install asserts two PROTECT policies reach the SPD; single-polarity annotated

RFC4301-4.4.1-10.note: Ordered search proven at the stack, both ways, over real XFRM in a rootless netns with two overlapping inbound entries whose kernel priorities the tests read back. Positive TestRFC4301OrderedInboundSearchAdmitsOnTheFirstRankedEntry: Child SA entry (priority 2000, allow) over the inbound catch-all DISCARD (2^32-1, block); an in-selector packet on the SA is delivered with XfrmInPolBlock +0, an out-of-selector packet meets only the catch-all and is dropped (+1). Negative TestRFC4301OrderedInboundSearchRefusesOnTheFirstRankedDiscard: an operator inbound DISCARD (spdPolicyParams, order 1000, read back as 1000 block) covering the Child SA selector drops an in-selector packet on the SA (XfrmInPolBlock +1, not delivered) although the later PROTECT template matches. Also: TestRFC4301ParallelSAs* (verification after decryption, XfrmInNoPols) and the SPD boundary units (priority carried). Minor: orderedInboundPriority returns the first kernel policy with the src/dst strings, which in the negative could be the Child SA entry; the Fatalf then fails loud, never passes wrongly. Re-judged 2026-09-30 (pass 3): the tagged units changed only by tag lines (RFC4301-4.4-1 and 4.4.2.1-1 lines deleted from the dataplane boundary units, RFC4301-5.2-2 lines added to the engine sad_selector units); bodies identical, verdict unchanged. Re-judged 2026-09-30 (leftovers): the two dataplane SPD boundary units changed only by tag lines (RFC4301-5.1-1 and RFC4301-5.2-3 lines, rows retired as lead-ins, moved to RFC4301-5.1-4 and RFC4301-5.2-2); bodies identical to HEAD, judge ran both: PASS; verdict unchanged.

RFC4301-4.4.1-11.note: Re-judged 2026-10-11 by an independent judge after the fix round (2691e815b1) added the disposition pair. RFC 4301 4.4.1, under "The SPD MUST permit a user or administrator to specify policy entries as follows:": "SPD-I: For inbound traffic that is to be bypassed or discarded, the entry consists of the values of the selectors that apply to the traffic to be bypassed or discarded." The engine units judged before (TestSPDPolicyMirrorsTheInboundSelector, TestRFC4301BypassReturnTrafficHasAnSPDIEntry, TestRFC4301BypassSPDIEntryIsNeverAnUnmirroredCopy) are unchanged and carry the selector half: the inbound entry holds the mirrored selectors of the traffic, never an unmirrored copy (records on spdPolicyParams). The added positive TestRFC4301SPDPermitsEachDispositionInEachDatabase carries the 'administrator can specify' half: bypass and discard with direction in and both parse through ParseIPsecConfig to the exact SPActionBypass/SPActionDiscard and SPDDirIn/SPDDirBoth; its claim names disposition and direction only, which is what it asserts. The added negative TestRFC4301SPDRefusesADispositionItDoesNotCarry refuses an absent action (not read as PROTECT, the SPAction zero value), protect, an unknown action and an unknown direction, each by its exact message. Revert records on ipsec/spd_policy.go::parseSPDPolicy for both.

RFC4301-4.4.1-12.note: Re-judged 2026-10-11 by an independent judge after the fix round (2691e815b1) added the disposition pair. RFC 4301 4.4.1, under "The SPD MUST permit a user or administrator to specify policy entries as follows:": "SPD-O: For outbound traffic that is to be bypassed or discarded, the entry consists of the values of the selectors that apply to the traffic to be bypassed or discarded." The engine units judged before (TestSPDPolicyMirrorsTheInboundSelector, TestRFC4301InboundBypassReturnTrafficHasAnSPDOEntry, TestRFC4301BypassSPDOEntryIsNeverAnUnmirroredCopy) are unchanged and carry the selector half (records on spdPolicyParams). The added positive TestRFC4301SPDPermitsEachDispositionInEachDatabase shows bypass and discard with direction out and both parse to the exact disposition and SPDDirOut/SPDDirBoth; its claim names disposition and direction only, which is what it asserts. The added negative TestRFC4301SPDRefusesADispositionItDoesNotCarry refuses an absent action, protect, an unknown action and an unknown direction by exact message. Revert records on ipsec/spd_policy.go::parseSPDPolicy for both.

RFC4301-4.4.1-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after 53370ab3be). RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1 read: 'Every SPD SHOULD have a nominal, final entry that matches anything that is otherwise unmatched, and discards it.' Producer path: ze-ipsec-conf.yang leaf unmatched `default discard`; ipsec/config.go parseUnmatched returns SPActionDiscard when the leaf is absent; applyConfig (apply.go) calls installUnmatched with cfg.Unmatched; unmatchedPolicies builds a wildcard-prefix, any-protocol, any-port entry at dataplane.PriorityUnmatched for in/out/fwd in both families. Positive (TestRFC4301DefaultFinalSPDEntryDiscards): leaf absent -> ParseIPsecConfig -> installUnmatched; asserts 6 entries at the final rank, discard action, /0 source and destination, UpperProto 0, any ports. This now covers the 'matches anything' clause the 90b90c0ae1 verdict found missing. Negative (TestRFC4301InboundClearPacketIsDiscardedByTheDefaultFinalEntry): leaf absent config parsed, its disposition installed by installUnmatched beside two operator SPD-I entries on real Linux XFRM in a user netns; a clear UDP datagram to a port no entry names is not delivered and XfrmInPolBlock rises by exactly 1. Run here unprivileged: both PASS, the netns child ran (no skip). Discrimination beyond the recorded panic breaks, by go test -overlay mutants: parseUnmatched absent->SPActionBypass turned BOTH tagged units red (action 1 want 2; datagram delivered); unmatchedPolicies UpperProto 6 turned both red; source prefix narrowed to /1 turned the positive red (the negative stays green, its claim does not cover prefixes). So the deciding logic, the default disposition and the wildcard selector, is proven in both polarities and the claims state no more than the assertions. Whole-stack scope: the paths with no catch-all at all (VPP backend, before the first apply, after engine exit) are carried as {gap} on RFC4301-5.2-1 and RFC4301-5.2-9 and do not touch this SHOULD's default disposition; a leaf-unset commit that would newly turn the discard on is refused (refuseImplicitDiscard) so the operator writes the leaf, and a daemon starting with the leaf unset installs the discard. Both tagged units changed in 53370ab3be (positive extended, negative new), so no upgrade_reason is owed.

RFC4301-4.4.1-4.note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent judge, after 4c41f84038, which replaced childPolicyParams with childPolicies: one inbound and one outbound policy per negotiated pair, all bound to the one SA, plus inboundStateSelector for the transport-mode state). RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1: "Thus, a user or administrator MUST be able to order the entries to express a desired access control policy." Prior verdict enforced. The tagged units changed only by childPolicyParams(x, dir) becoming childPolicies(x, dir)[0]; their fixtures carry no selector set, so childPolicies returns exactly one policy and [0] is the same SPParams as before. childPairPolicy resolves Priority from child.PolicyPriority (zero to PriorityChildSA) for every pair, so a multi-pair Child SA carries the operator's rank on every policy. Assertions unchanged: operator rank reaches both directions and orders overlapping peers; unstated order is not 0 and a rekey keeps the default rank; an order capturing IKE is refused (engine and ipsec). All PASS at HEAD. Verdict stands. Owed by the author: the revert record on TestSpdOperatorOrdersOverlappingPeers names childPolicyParams and no longer verifies (unit-changed); re-record it on childPolicies.

RFC4301-4.4.1-6.note: Re-judged 2026-10-11 by an independent judge after the fix round (2691e815b1) moved the two disposition tests off this row. RFC 4301 4.4.1, under "The SPD MUST permit a user or administrator to specify policy entries as follows:": "SPD-S: For traffic that is to be protected using IPsec, the entry consists of the values of the selectors that apply to the traffic to be protected via AH or ESP, controls on how to create SAs based on these selectors, and the parameters needed to effect this protection (e.g., algorithms, modes, etc.)." The row now carries only the SPD-S pair, both unchanged since the last read: TestRFC4301SPDSEntryCarriesSelectorsSAControlsAndProtection parses a site-to-site peer through ParseIPsecConfig and ValidateGroupRefs and reads back the selector prefixes, the SA creation controls (connection-type, remote address, esp-group) and the protection parameters (mode transport, aes256/sha256), each compared exactly; TestRFC4301SPDSEntryRefusesAMissingOrUnusablePart refuses an undefined esp-group, mode beet, an unknown connection-type and a /33 selector, each naming the part. Revert records on config.go::parseSiteToSitePeer. The earlier defect (bypass/discard tests tagged here) is resolved.

RFC4301-4.4.1.2-1.note: Independent source rejudgment against complete RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1.2: ‘An SPD is an ordered list of entries each of which contains the following fields.’ The assigned complete item is: ‘One to N selector sets that correspond to the "condition" for applying a particular IPsec action.’ internal/component/ike/ipsec/config.go::ParseIPsecConfig calls parseSPDPolicies, and internal/component/ike/ipsec/spd_policy.go::parseSPDPolicy constructs one SPDPolicy with one local/remote prefix, one protocol and one port pair. N=1 satisfies this structural item; this does not prove the separately allocated users-MUST-NOT rule or multi-selector negotiation. Read both tagged units and their helpers in internal/component/ike/ipsec/rfc4301_selector_set_test.go. TestRFC4301SPDEntryHoldsOneSelectorSet parses an actual config tree and checks both exact prefixes, protocol 17, local port value 53 and remote ANY. TestRFC4301SPDEntryCannotCarryASecondSelectorSet checks the returned model for selector-bearing collections and exactly four scalar prefix/port fields. The latter is a structural guard, not an exhaustive validator of hypothetical future nested models. The single-positive annotation is justified for the one-set representation, which has no selectable zero-set/multiple-set cardinality; it does not mean malformed configurations have no refusal paths. The enum-owned edits are ordinary exhaustive comments in the test and holdsSelector, outside the tag claim. They stale the audit unit but do not themselves change discrimination behavior or claim hashes; the canonical scope report records the tagged comment-only cover as verified. No new execution or baseline-freshness claim.

RFC4301-4.4.2-1.note: Judged at the whole stack (R21). Transport: installChildSA now sets the inbound SAParams.Sel from childPolicyParams(child, SADirIn) (src=TSr, dst=TSi, proto, sport/dport, direction checked with asymmetric ports 179/any in TestRFC4301InboundSADEntryCarriesTheNegotiatedSelectors), mapped to x->sel by xfrmStateFromParams. Tunnel: the inbound require-policy carries the same five. Kernel probes in rfc4301_sad_selector_linux_test.go (user+net namespace, real XFRM) assert delivery inside and exact +1 on XfrmInNoPols (tunnel: outside by source, port, protocol) or XfrmInStateMismatch (transport: port, protocol) with no delivery. Judge re-observed red under two overlays: transport Sel block disabled -> port 6000 delivered, counters 0; inbound tunnel policy widened -> all three outside cases delivered, NoPols 0. The multi-pair 'or values' half is the gap RFC4301-4.4.2-2. Re-judged 2026-09-30 (pass 3): the tagged units changed only by tag lines (RFC4301-4.4-1 and 4.4.2.1-1 lines deleted from the dataplane boundary units, RFC4301-5.2-2 lines added to the engine sad_selector units); bodies identical, verdict unchanged.

RFC4301-4.4.2-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent judge, after 4c41f84038, which replaced childPolicyParams with childPolicies: one inbound and one outbound policy per negotiated pair, all bound to the one SA, plus inboundStateSelector for the transport-mode state). RFC 4301 Section 4.4.2: "For each of the selectors defined in Section 4.4.1.1, the entry for an inbound SA in the SAD MUST be initially populated with the value or values negotiated at the time the SA was created." Prior verdict unimplemented (only Selectors[0] reached the dataplane). At HEAD, childPolicies builds one policy per pair in child.Selectors in both directions with that pair's prefixes, protocol (pair.I.Proto) and ports (selectorPort per side), every one carrying the child's ReqID/SAID; installChildSA installs all inbound then all outbound and rolls back what it installed on failure; removal, MOBIKE migration and samePolicySelector take the whole set. Tunnel mode: the state carries no selector and the per-pair require-policies with the SA's template are the entry's selectors, so every negotiated value is populated exactly (interop responder-two-subnets shows both pairs' policies on both kernels; TestRFC4301EveryNegotiatedPairGetsAPolicyPerDirection, untagged, PASS). Transport mode: one XFRM state holds one selector, so inboundStateSelector writes the narrowest single selector covering every pair (coverPrefix per side, protocol to any and ports to any when pairs differ; exact for one pair; TestRFC4301TransportStateSelectorCoversEveryPair and TestCoverPrefixIsTheLongestCommonPrefix, untagged, PASS). With several pairs whose union is not one selector the SAD entry therefore holds a superset of the values negotiated, so the {gap} stands, narrowed. Finding on the gap text: it conditions the delivery on `unmatched bypass`, but a decrypted transport-mode packet in the cover and in no pair is decided by the FIRST SPD-I entry it matches, which can be the IKE bypass (PriorityIKEBypass 100, UDP 500/4500 between the endpoints, which in transport mode are the inner addresses) or an operator `vpn ipsec policy` BYPASS entry (any order above 100, searched before the catch-all at PriorityUnmatched); an allow entry with no template accepts a transport-mode secpath, so such a packet is delivered under `unmatched discard` too (reasoned from Linux __xfrm_policy_check/secpath_has_nontransport, not observed by a test). The gap should say the entry is a superset regardless of the unmatched leaf and name every BYPASS entry that can then deliver. Transport pairs of two address families make coverPrefix refuse and the install fail with a named error, not widen. Row carries {gap}; the implemented scope (tunnel mode, single-pair transport) would be better expressed as {partial} with this residual as Gap, which the author may propose. No tests tag the row.

RFC4301-4.4.2.1-1.note: Row now quotes the SPI item alone (split, Correction 2026-09-30). Positive TestRFC4301SADItemSPIIsTheNegotiatedValue: inbound and outbound SAD entries carry the SPI given, unchanged. Negative TestRFC4301SADItemZeroSPIIsRefused: SPI 0 (RFC 4303 section 2.1: reserved, MUST NOT be sent on the wire, so it identifies no SA) builds no state; the refusal is the D-8 fix in xfrmStateFromParams. Unit-level over the builder; both records observed red.

RFC4301-4.4.2.1-10.note: Positive: AES-GCM entry carries the AEAD algorithm, ICV 128 and key, and neither separate transform. Negative: unknown combined-mode algorithm refused, no state. Builder-level.

RFC4301-4.4.2.1-11.note: Both halves of the row now proven. Interval: the pass-4 units (newLifetimeState, the producer established.go uses) prove hard = build + configured lifetime with soft (replace) before hard (terminate). Indication of which action: the owner-loop units drive the real maintainSA over one tick. Positive: soft past, hard far -> a CREATE_CHILD_SA request on the wire, loop alive, pendingRekey kind rekeyChild naming the old Child SA with a new non-zero inbound SPI (replace with a new SA and new SPI). Negative: soft far, hard past -> loop returns errTimeout, no pendingRekey, Child SA cleared, old inbound SPI removed from the dataplane, silence on the wire (terminate). Revert records on established.go::maintainSA observed red for both; the author's soft/hard swap overlay turned both red, so the pair discriminates the mapping, not only the loop's existence.

RFC4301-4.4.2.1-12.note: Positive: tunnel and transport each installed as their own kernel mode. Negative: a mode that is neither refused, no state. Builder-level.

RFC4301-4.4.2.1-18.note: Positive: IPv4 and IPv6 tunnel header pairs read back unchanged. Negative: IPv4 source with IPv6 destination refused, no state (D-8 fix in xfrmStateFromParams). No legitimate caller builds a mixed pair: engine SAs use the IKE endpoints, OSPF SAs are transport. Builder-level.

RFC4301-4.4.2.1-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after c85342c940). Section 4.4.2.1 lifetime item (a): "If byte count is used, then the implementation SHOULD count the number of bytes ... Note that implementations MUST be able to handle having the counters at the ends of an SA get out of synch". The row is now {gap} and no test tags it: the two SAD boundary tags, which asserted the anti-replay window and were recorded wrong, were moved off by owner ruling. The gap is real: newLifetimeState (internal/component/ike/engine/rekey.go) sets softTime and hardTime only, lifetimeState.softBytes and byteCount are never written by non-test code, and xfrmStateFromParams installs no byte limit, so Ze keeps no byte-count lifetime whose counters could fall out of synch. The obligation is conditional on byte-count lifetimes, whose absence is the RFC4301-4.4.2.1-2 gap; scheduled in plan/spec-ipsec-lifetime-volume.md. Recording this gap authorizes no implementation.

RFC4301-4.4.2.1-4.note: Single-polarity positive (justified: Ze negotiates ESN 'not extended' only, which the item permits 'if negotiated', so no input selects another width). The SAD entry carries no ESN flag and no preset replay state. Builder-level.

RFC4301-4.4.2.1-5.note: Single-polarity positive accepted: no config leaf or negotiation offers rollover or ESN. The unit builds ESP and AH SAs in both directions through xfrmStateFromParams and asserts OSeqMayWrap and ESN unset, so the kernel (xfrm_replay_overflow) audits the overflow and stops transmission. Would go red if the producer set rollover. Record: revert xfrmStateFromParams, observed red. Judge finding (not fixed): the stop-not-rollover decision is the zero value of netlink.XfrmState.OSeqMayWrap and xfrmStateFromParams never names it; under the principles rule a zero another component relies on is a guard that must be named (explicit assignment with the RFC quote). The test pins it, so it cannot vanish silently, but the producer still owes the named guard.

RFC4301-4.4.2.1-6.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after c85342c940). Section 4.4.2.1: "Anti-Replay Window: a 64-bit counter and a bit-map (or equivalent) used to determine whether an inbound AH or ESP packet is a replay." TestRFC4301BoundarySADEntryCarriesWhatTheKernelLooksUp changed only by the deleted RFC4301-4.4.2.1-3 tag line; body identical, it asserts ReplayWindow == 64 on the entry xfrmStateFromParams builds (internal/component/ike/dataplane/xfrm_linux.go sets state.ReplayWindow from p.ReplayWin). TestRFC4301SADItemAntiReplayWindowIsInstalled reads windows 32 and 64 back. Builder-level, zero not asserted; the kernel performs the replay check on the window Ze installs. Single polarity as annotated: every window is installed as given.

RFC4301-4.4.2.1-7.note: AH in scope (OSPFv3, RFC 4552). Positive: AH entry carries integrity algorithm, 128-bit truncation, the given key, no crypt/aead. Negative: unknown integrity algorithm refused, no state. Builder-level.

RFC4301-4.4.2.1-8.note: Positive: ESP entry carries the encryption algorithm and the given key (distinct from the integrity key). Negative: unknown encryption algorithm refused, no state. Builder-level.

RFC4301-4.4.2.1-9.note: Positive: ESP entry carries the integrity algorithm, truncation and the given key. Negative: unknown integrity algorithm refused, no state. Builder-level.

RFC4301-4.4.3.1-1.note: sub-tree entries admit DNS, RFC 822 and DN peers beneath them and refuse near misses, apex and outside peers; certificate binding kept

RFC4301-4.4.3.1-2.note: prefix PAD entries admit addresses inside for v4 and v6 and refuse outside, other family and text spellings; the same prefix syntax the SPD uses

RFC4301-4.4.3.1-3.note: ID_KEY_ID admitted only on octet-exact equality; prefix, suffix, case, trailing dot and sub-tree variants refused

RFC4301-4.4.3.2-1.note: with remote-id set, a certificate carrying the asserted ID (SAN, or CN without SAN) is admitted and one issued to another name is refused naming the asserted ID

RFC4301-4.5-1.note: automated half: createFirstChildSA installs IKE-keyed SAs; manual half: OSPFv3 installs static SPI+key SAs; single-polarity annotated

RFC4301-4.5.2-1.note: encryption key asserted as the leading octets and integrity key the following octets per SA, and the swapped split asserted absent

RFC4301-4.5.3-1.note: gateway address and destination ranges parsed as written; malformed range refused naming peer and range

RFC4301-5.1-4.note: Step 2 (match the outbound packet headers against the SPD). Linux keeps no SPD cache, so the match is the kernel SPD lookup over the entries Ze installs through createFirstChildSA, installSPDPolicies and installUnmatched. Positive: from one source, a datagram to 10.1.0.5 meets the Child SA PROTECT entry (ESP at the tunnel endpoint under child.OutboundSPI, XfrmOutNoStates unchanged) and one to 10.3.0.5:7001 meets the operator BYPASS entry (delivered clear, no ESP). Negative: 10.3.0.5 on port 7009, differing from the BYPASS entry only by port, is not bypassed: EPERM, XfrmOutPolBlock +1, not delivered, so the match reads the headers, not the destination alone. Judge ran both units in their own user+net namespace: PASS, not skipped. Records: xfrmPolicyFromParams panic revert red both polarities; author's manual overlays (bypass->BLOCK reddens the positive, discard->ALLOW reddens the negative, scratch p7-ov-*.log) confirm each polarity reads the disposition. Re-judged 2026-09-30 (leftovers): the retired lead-in RFC4301-5.1-1's tags moved here onto the dataplane SPD boundary units, as supplementary builder-level cover of step 2's input: the positive asserts the outbound entry's out direction, 10.0.0.0/24 -> 10.1.0.0/24 prefixes and exact source port 443; the negative asserts a 0x00ff port mask is refused (nil policy) for SADirOut and SADirIn rather than widened. Claims match the assertions. Records: xfrmPolicyFromParams panic revert observed red both polarities. Judge ran both: PASS. Stack proof stays the two engine units.

RFC4301-5.1-5.note: Step 3a: process as the matching entry says, BYPASS, DISCARD or PROTECT. PROTECT: the datagram reaches the remote endpoint as ESP carrying the Child SA outbound SPI, no XfrmOutNoStates. BYPASS: delivered in the clear, and no ESP copy on the raw socket. DISCARD: operator DISCARD entry refuses the write with EPERM, XfrmOutPolBlock +1, not delivered. All three dispositions asserted on kernel counters and delivery; AH is not installed by IKE (ESP only), so the PROTECT case is ESP. Records: producer revert red both polarities; overlays discard->ALLOW and bypass->BLOCK each redden exactly the unit that asserts that disposition.

RFC4301-5.1-6.note: Step 3b SPD search. With no kernel SPD cache every packet, including the first of a flow, is looked up in the SPD (SPD-S: the Child SA PROTECT entry; SPD-O: operator BYPASS/DISCARD and the catch-all). Positive: first packets on the PROTECT and BYPASS entries take those entries' dispositions. Negative: a packet selecting no operator entry takes the catch-all's discard (EPERM, XfrmOutPolBlock +1), not a neighbouring entry's bypass. Claims name the cache absence rather than proving a cache. Records as 5.1-4.

RFC4301-5.1-7.note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent judge, after 4c41f84038, which replaced childPolicyParams with childPolicies: one inbound and one outbound policy per negotiated pair, all bound to the one SA, plus inboundStateSelector for the transport-mode state). RFC 4301 Section 5.1: "If the SPD entry calls for PROTECT, i.e., creation of an SA, the key management mechanism (e.g., IKEv2) is invoked to create the SA." Prior verdict unimplemented. installChildSA changed only to install one policy per negotiated pair; PROTECT entries are still installed only beside an already negotiated Child SA, parseSPDPolicy still refuses an operator protect entry, and no Go file under internal/, cmd/ or pkg/ references XfrmMonitor or XFRMNLGRP_ACQUIRE (grep 2026-10-19), so no outbound packet invokes IKEv2. The {gap} text (createFirstChildSA, no acquire handling) remains accurate. Gap stands.

RFC4301-5.2-1.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after 79aaa4fe34). RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1 read: 'Since the SPD-I is just a part of the SPD, if a packet that is looked up in the SPD-I cannot be matched to an entry there, then the packet MUST be discarded.' With the default now discard, the installed-catch-all path conforms on XFRM (every inbound packet meets the PriorityUnmatched entry, and the kernel blocks it: untagged TestRFC4301InboundClearPacketMatchingNoEntryFollowsTheUnmatchedLeaf PASS in a user netns). Under a written `unmatched bypass` the packet matches a bypass entry, so this sentence is not engaged. The {gap} stays truthful, re-verified at the producers: (a) VPP: vppPolicyInterface refuses IfIndex 0, so verifyUnmatchedEnforceable refuses the default discard at commit and installUnmatched fails the startup apply; only `unmatched bypass` runs there, and installUnmatched then installs nothing (logged), leaving no SPD-I entry; (b) before the first applyConfig and after removeUnmatched at engine exit no catch-all exists; (c) a bypass install failure or a platform without XFRM is logged and tolerated (under bypass only; under the default discard both fail the apply). Reader note: the annotation's '(c) ... a platform without XFRM, is logged and tolerated' holds only under `unmatched bypass` and could say so. Not counted conformant.

RFC4301-5.2-10.note: Step 4 first sentence: ESP processing with the SAD entry step 3a selected. Positive: the packet on the Child SA SPI is decrypted with that SA's key and delivered, XfrmInStateProtoError unchanged. Negative: right SPI, fresh sequence number, sealed with a zero key: ICV fails, XfrmInStateProtoError +1, not delivered, so processing uses the selected SA's key and not a pass-through. Judge ran both: PASS. Records: xfrmStateFromParams revert red both. AH processing (OSPFv3) not probed here.

RFC4301-5.2-2.note: Whole stack over real XFRM in a rootless netns (R23: the kernel performs the check on the state and policy Ze installs). Tunnel: an inner packet inside the negotiated selectors is delivered; outside by source, port or protocol each moves XfrmInNoPols by 1 and is not delivered. Transport: inside delivered; outside by port or protocol each moves XfrmInStateMismatch by 1. Records observed red on childPolicyParams and installChildSA. Re-judged 2026-09-30 (leftovers): the retired lead-in RFC4301-5.2-3's tags moved here onto the dataplane SPD boundary units, supplementary builder-level cover of the step 4 selector check's input: positive asserts the inbound entry's in direction, the outbound entry's source prefix, exact source port 443 and one template; negative asserts the inexpressible port mask is refused for SADirIn (and SADirOut). The RFC names the selectors 'identified by the SAD entry'; on Linux that check is the inbound require-policy plus template match against the SA, so the policy selector is the right boundary. Records: xfrmPolicyFromParams panic revert observed red both polarities. Judge ran both: PASS.

RFC4301-5.2-6.note: Step 3a SAD lookup of an ESP packet addressed to Ze. Positive: ESP on the Child SA inbound SPI, sealed with the kernel key around an inner packet inside the selectors, is delivered with XfrmInNoStates and XfrmInStateProtoError unchanged. Negative: the same packet under SPI^0x5a5a5a5a finds nothing (XfrmInNoStates +1, not delivered), so the lookup is keyed on the SPI. Judge ran both: PASS in own namespace. Records: xfrmStateFromParams panic revert red both polarities. Scope: ESP, unicast; the AH case (OSPFv3 manual SAs) is the same kernel lookup and is not probed here.

RFC4301-5.2-7.note: Step 3a no-match discard. Negative: an ESP packet on an SPI no SA holds is counted XfrmInNoStates +1 and never delivered. Positive: the same packet on the installed SPI is delivered, so the discard is the SAD miss and not a blanket drop. Unicast probed here; the multicast lookup miss (SPI+group) is proven under RFC4301-4.1-6 (ospf rfc4301_multicast_sa_linux_test.go) as a kernel SAD lookup, not a delivered-packet probe. Records: xfrmStateFromParams revert red both polarities.

RFC4301-5.2-8.note: Step 3b SPD-I lookup of a clear packet addressed to Ze. Positive: UDP from 10.3.0.5 to local port 7101 matches the operator in-BYPASS entry ranked ahead of a DISCARD catch-all: delivered, no XfrmInPolBlock. Negative: to port 7102 on the operator in-DISCARD entry with a BYPASS catch-all: XfrmInPolBlock +1, not delivered, so only the matched entry can have dropped it. Each unit isolates its disposition by the opposite catch-all. Judge ran both: PASS. Records: xfrmPolicyFromParams revert red both; overlays bypass->BLOCK / discard->ALLOW redden exactly the matching polarity (scratch p7-ovin-*.log). Not-addressed-to-device (forwarded) packets are not probed; the SPD-I lookup is the same fwd/in policy check.

RFC4301-5.2-9.note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after 79aaa4fe34). RFC 4301 Section 5.2 step 3b read: '(No SAs are created in response to receipt of a packet that requires IPsec protection; only BYPASS or DISCARD cache entries can be created this way.) If there is no match, discard the traffic.' Same producer walk as RFC4301-5.2-1: with the catch-all installed (default discard after 79aaa4fe34) an inbound clear packet no operator entry names is blocked by the kernel (untagged TestRFC4301InboundClearPacketMatchingNoEntryFollowsTheUnmatchedLeaf, PASS here), but the no-entry paths remain: VPP (runs only under `unmatched bypass`, which installs nothing there), before the first apply and after engine exit (removeUnmatched), and a tolerated bypass install failure or no-XFRM platform. The {gap} annotation still describes the code. No tag carries this id, correctly. Not counted conformant.

RFC4301-7.1-2.note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent judge, after 4c41f84038, which replaced childPolicyParams with childPolicies: one inbound and one outbound policy per negotiated pair, all bound to the one SA, plus inboundStateSelector for the transport-mode state). RFC 4301 Section 7.1: "If the SA will carry traffic for specified protocols, the selector set for the SA MUST specify the port fields (or ICMP type/code or Mobility Header type) as ANY." Prior verdict enforced. selectorPort now takes the side (tsSelector) instead of (child, local); childPolicies picks local/remote by SelectorsLocalIsTSi exactly as the old side choice did, and the ANY/single/OPAQUE mapping is byte-identical. The units changed only to childPolicies(rfc4301ChildWith(pair), dir)[0]; rfc4301ChildWith carries one pair, so the slice holds one policy. Each negotiated pair now gets its own protocol and ports, so a multi-pair SA no longer inherits pair 0's. Positive asserts UpperProto 17 and both ports ANY in both directions; negative asserts no ExactPortMatch(8080/9090/0) leaks under ANY. PASS at HEAD. Verdict stands. Owed: both revert records (break on selectorPort) report unit-changed and must be re-observed.

RFC4301-7.1-3.note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent judge, after 4c41f84038, which replaced childPolicyParams with childPolicies: one inbound and one outbound policy per negotiated pair, all bound to the one SA, plus inboundStateSelector for the transport-mode state). RFC 4301 Section 7.1: "If the SA will carry traffic without regard to a specific protocol value (i.e., ANY is specified as the (Next Layer) protocol selector value), then the port field values are undefined and MUST be set to ANY as well." Prior verdict enforced. TestRFC4301ProtocolAnyChildSACarriesAnyPorts changed only to childPolicies(child, dir)[0] over a one-pair narrowing result; it still asserts UpperProto 0 and both ports ANY in and out. The negative (programmableSelector refuses protocol ANY with a port) and the ipsec supplementary units are unchanged. The new transport-state cover also widens ports to ANY whenever the protocol widens to any (inboundStateSelector), consistent with this sentence. PASS at HEAD. Verdict stands. Owed: the positive's revert record (break on selectorPort) reports unit-changed and must be re-observed.

RFC4301-7.3-4.note: Forbidden: accepting a non-initial fragment on an SA with non-trivial port selectors (Ze has no NON_FIRST_FRAGMENTS_ALSO negotiation). Ze's boundary is the inbound XFRM policy the kernel checks; Linux decodes no ports for a non-initial fragment, so an exact port selector refuses it. TestRFC4301BoundarySPDEntryCarriesSelectorDirectionOrderAndTemplate asserts in.SrcPort == 443 on the inbound entry, red if the selector is widened to ANY. TestRFC4301BoundarySPDEntryIsRefusedRatherThanWidened asserts a partial mask (0x00ff) is refused for SADirIn and SADirOut, red if it is installed widened. Re-judged 2026-09-30: the two SPD boundary units changed only by the deleted RFC4301-4.4.1-9 tag lines (row retired, decorrelation is optional and Ze never decorrelates); bodies identical, verdict unchanged. Re-judged 2026-09-30 (pass 3): the tagged units changed only by tag lines (RFC4301-4.4-1 and 4.4.2.1-1 lines deleted from the dataplane boundary units, RFC4301-5.2-2 lines added to the engine sad_selector units); bodies identical, verdict unchanged. Re-judged 2026-09-30 (leftovers): the two dataplane SPD boundary units changed only by tag lines (RFC4301-5.1-1 and RFC4301-5.2-3 lines, rows retired as lead-ins, moved to RFC4301-5.1-4 and RFC4301-5.2-2); bodies identical to HEAD, judge ran both: PASS; verdict unchanged.

RFC4301-7.3-5.note: Whole stack over real XFRM in a rootless netns, tunnel-mode Child SA on UDP 10.1.0.0/16 -> 10.2.0.0/16 port 5000. Positive TestRFC4301FragmentsOfACompliantPacketAreDelivered: an in-selector inner packet split into initial and non-initial fragments, each in its own ESP packet, non-initial first: reassembled and delivered, XfrmInNoPols +0. Negative TestRFC4301FragmentsOfANonCompliantPacketAreDiscarded: same with inner source outside the selector: the non-initial fragment is discarded with the packet (XfrmInNoPols +1, nothing delivered). Linux reassembles before the inbound policy check, so the discard is the stack acting on the require-policy Ze installs. The violating dimension is the source address, which the fragment itself carries; a port-only violation (the fragment-specific hazard) is covered by RFC4301-7.3-4. The SPD boundary tags stay as supplementary; their negative (bypass carries no template) proves a neighbour. Re-judged 2026-09-30 (pass 3): the tagged units changed only by tag lines (RFC4301-4.4-1 and 4.4.2.1-1 lines deleted from the dataplane boundary units, RFC4301-5.2-2 lines added to the engine sad_selector units); bodies identical, verdict unchanged. Re-judged 2026-09-30 (leftovers): the two dataplane SPD boundary units changed only by tag lines (RFC4301-5.1-1 and RFC4301-5.2-3 lines, rows retired as lead-ins, moved to RFC4301-5.1-4 and RFC4301-5.2-2); bodies identical to HEAD, judge ran both: PASS; verdict unchanged.
